finding.claim: The /logo handler fetches a user-supplied URL after only a substring check for "example.io". That check does not constrain scheme, host or port. An attacker can use http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/?x=example.io, http://example.io@127.0.0.1:8080/, or http://attacker.com/example.io. The response body is streamed back to the caller, so this is a full-read SSRF. Redirects are followed because http.Get uses the default client.
finding.sink: http.Get(raw) at main.go:36, with the response body copied to the client at main.go:38

trace.note: strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") is the only validation, a substring match on the whole URL string
http.Get(raw) fetches the unparsed, unvalidated URL with the default client, which follows redirects
io.Copy(w, resp.Body) returns the fetched body to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: The only guard is the substring check at line 32. It is bypassable through the path, query, userinfo or a subdomain of an attacker domain. There is no scheme check, no host allowlist, no resolved-IP check and no redirect restriction. The default client also follows redirects, so an allowed host that redirects can reach internal targets.

verdict.guard_found: Only strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") at main.go:32, a substring check that does not close the finding. The strict trusted-host check at main.go:20 applies only to the separate /cdn handler.
verdict.reason: main.go:31 takes the user-controlled "logo" form value, main.go:32 only substring-matches "example.io", and main.go:36 passes the raw string to http.Get, whose default client follows redirects, with the body copied to the caller at main.go:38.
